Alex K: heads-up — we've got a customer p99 spike on text-generation-prod-us, ticket CI-4521 opened by Support. p50/p95 fine, p99 jumped from 320ms to 1.8s around 15:02 UTC.
Maria D: saw the alert, digging into per-route metrics now. looks like sustained increase starting ~15:00.
OpsBot: [ALERT] route=text-generation-prod-us p99_latency > 1.5s for 3m (triggered at 2026-03-15T15:03:12Z)
Jamal S: any config changes around that time? deploys?
Tara L: no deploys on runtime cluster. but I see a config push to continuous-batcher defaults at 14:58 — someone enabled "auto_expand_hold" for microbatching to optimize cost.
Alex K: that matches. change: continuous-batcher.auto_expand_hold=true + hold_window_ms=200 default. intended to reduce ops costs for tiny prompts.
Maria D: hypothesis: small prompts arriving in high QPS create lots of microbatches, auto_expand increases hold windows to aggregate, which might hurt when a single long request arrives (long generation) and gets queued behind tiny prompt batches -> head-of-line blocking.
Jamal S: can we reproduce quickly? I can run a traffic mix local against canary with 90% tiny prompts (10-20 tokens) + 10% long prompts (800-1200 tokens).
Tara L: please do. repro steps we used:
```
# spike test
for i in {1..900}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}' &
done
for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"long text ...","max_tokens":900}' &
done
```
Run against canary node with continuous-batcher metrics exported.
```
# check batcher metrics
kubectl logs -l app=continuous-batcher -c batcher --since=10m | grep "batch_size" | tail -n 200
```

Alex K: jamal ran it and confirmed: p50 ~ 300ms, p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1.7s. traces show long queuing before actual generation. trace_id=tr-0a1b2c3d.
OpsBot: trace tr-0a1b2c3d links: https://apm.redwood/dev/trace/tr-0a1b2c3d
Maria D: stack traces show many tiny batches (size=1-2) being flushed normally but hold_window expanded to 200ms so when long request arrives it waits behind several of those batches. tail latency dominated by queuing delays.
Jamal S: workaround options: 1) rollback auto_expand_hold flag (fast config toggle) 2) reduce hold_window_ms globally back to 20ms 3) implement fast-path priority for requests with estimated_long=true header 4) early-flush on detection of long-request token estimate.
Tara L: for immediate mitigation I'd prefer rollback to previous config (auto_expand_hold=false) — lowest blast radius. can someone flip it and confirm metrics?
Alex K: I'm bumping a config rollback now. patch:
```
# rollback
rbacctl set-config continuous-batcher.auto_expand_hold false --env=prod
rbacctl set-config continuous-batcher.hold_window_ms 20 --env=prod
```
Applying...
OpsBot: deploybot: config update applied by Alex K at 2026-03-15T15:12:46Z to cluster=prod.
Maria D: re-checking metrics — 5m after rollback p99 dropped to 380ms, p95 430ms -> looks like rollback effective.
Jamal S: good. we should still track because this may come back if someone re-enables auto_expand in the future.
Tara L: agreed. next steps:
- short term: rollback stays in place for 24h and don't re-enable without canary test
- medium term: add per-route dynamic hold policy and token-estimate header so router can prioritize large jobs
- long term: add congestion-aware batching that avoids head-of-line blocking by classifying requests by estimated output length

Alex K: adding repro notes to CI-4521 and will attach the curl script + canary dashboard.
Maria D: I've created an alert suppression for auto_expand toggles to require a two-person approval. ticket CI-4522.
Jamal S: sketch of a quick mitigation we can ship fast: detect requests with header `X-Estimated-Tokens` > 200 and tag them as high-priority; batcher will flush small batches ahead if high-priority present. minimal change to code.
Tara L: can we add a config flag continuous-batcher.priority_by_estimate but default=false? then we can enable on the problematic route only.
Alex K: sounds good. Jamal, please prototype PR with tests and a simulation harness. aim for canary tomorrow.
Jamal S: on it. I'll write sim to prove no regression on cost for majority tiny prompts.
Support Bot: note: customer CI-4521 updated — they were notified of mitigation and rollback. they reported initial improvement but asked for postmortem.
Maria D: will draft short postmortem: cause=auto_expand_hold + high tiny-prompt QPS leading to queueing + head-of-line blocking; impact=p99 spike for route text-generation-prod-us for ~12m; mitigation=rollback; next_steps=priority header, canary & approval gating.
Tara L: also add runbook entry: when p99 spike and p95 unaffected, check for batching hold_window changes and presence of many size=1 batches.
Alex K: thank you all. Jamal, ping when PR ready. I'll close the support loop once PM approves postmortem. :thumbsup:
Jamal S: PR drafted -> https://git.internal/redwood/continuous-batcher/pull/834 ; includes unit sims + benchmark results. schedule canary at 10:00 UTC tomorrow.
Maria D: logging note: we should emit metrics for "queue_wait_ms" per request and a tag for estimated_token_bucket so dashboards can slice by token size. I'll file infra ticket.
Tara L: awesome. mark CI-4521 resolved for now.
Support Bot: CI-4521 status -> mitigated.
Alex K: closing thread — followups in CI-4522 and PR 834.
